newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa SAA sees over 350 mln rand 1996/97 loss.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa SAA sees over 350 mln rand 1996/97 loss.

text.p: State-run South African Airways said on Tuesday it was facing a loss of more than 350 million rand for the financial year ended March 1997.
"(The full-year loss) should be above 350 million rand," Transnet executive director Zukile Nomvete told Reuters.
"A lot of things happened, the rand fell, the cost of fuel (rose)," he added.
SAA is part of the Transnet parastatal.
Nomvete said the airline had budgeted 960 million rand for fuel, but had spent almost 1.2 billion rand by year-end.
He said the airline also had lost money because it was unable to fly domestic routes using international flights.
